name: Continuous rice, winter flood
tagline: What the field does today: rice every year, flooded over winter for straw and waterfowl.

exposed_rain_days.note: Days with heavy rain (≥ 25–50 mm) while the field is less than half covered and not flooded

why.text: This is the baseline every alternative is compared against: rice from May to early October, then a winter flood.
why.author: template

evidence.text: Satellite cover shows rice in 9 of the last 10 years; 2022 was fallow.
evidence.author: template

gaps: Rice flood and percolation water is an estimate until cited.

name: Rice + winter cover (no winter flood)
tagline: Keep rice; drill a cereal/vetch cover after straw chop instead of re-flooding.

exposed_rain_days.note: Days with heavy rain (≥ 25–50 mm) while the field is less than half covered and not flooded

exposure.cover_basis: modelled cover from the crop calendar

source.title: USDA NRCS EQIP, practice 340 Cover Crop

rate_per_acre_usd.note: Payment rate not yet confirmed; ask the local NRCS office

why.text: Your field is typically bare from mid-October to late April unless it is flooded, which is when the heaviest rain arrives.
why.author: llm

why.text: A cereal/vetch cover drilled after straw chop keeps the soil covered through that window and cuts bare days from about 62 to about 36 a year.
why.author: llm

why.text: Skipping the winter flood lowers the season's irrigation need from roughly 1,340 mm to 1,120 mm (4.4 to 3.7 acre-ft/acre).
why.author: llm

why.text: Rice timing stays the same: half of fields are planted by 12 May on average, and harvest runs late September into October.
why.author: llm

evidence.text: Cover calendar 2016–2025: bare or unknown in 22–30 winter weeks of non-flood years; rule and ML detectors agree on 93% of weeks.
evidence.author: llm

evidence.text: 2022: the block was fallow all year, when Sacramento Valley rice acreage was roughly halved.
evidence.author: llm

evidence.text: OpenET measured rice ET of about 1,105 mm for the season; our modelled crop water use is within 4% of it.
evidence.author: llm

evidence.text: Soil is poorly drained silty clay (hydrologic group D): expect a limited infiltration gain from any rotation.
evidence.author: llm

gaps: Cover-crop species and seeding date after rice are not yet backed by a California trial result.
Rice flood and percolation water is an estimate until cited.
Vetch nitrogen credit to the following rice crop is not quantified.

name: Dry-year plan: fallow with cover or safflower
tagline: When allocation drops under 50%: skip rice, plant safflower in April or hold a cover.

exposed_rain_days.note: Days with heavy rain (≥ 25–50 mm) while the field is less than half covered and not flooded

exposure.cover_basis: modelled cover from the crop calendar

why.text: In a year like 2022, when allocations were cut and the block sat fallow, safflower planted in April uses a fraction of the water rice needs.
why.author: llm

why.text: Irrigation need is about 380 mm (1.2 acre-ft/acre) against about 1,340 mm for rice.
why.author: llm

evidence.text: Safflower stage lengths of 20/35/45/25 days from an April planting in California.
evidence.author: llm

gaps: Local safflower market and contract availability unknown.

name: Rice–winter wheat
tagline: Alternate rice with a winter wheat year drilled in Nov–Dec and cut in June.

exposed_rain_days.note: Days with heavy rain (≥ 25–50 mm) while the field is less than half covered and not flooded

exposure.cover_basis: modelled cover from the crop calendar

why.text: Winter wheat grows on winter rain and covers the field from December through May, the months your field is usually bare.
why.author: llm

why.text: In the wheat year irrigation need is about 240 mm (0.8 acre-ft/acre).
why.author: llm

evidence.text: Wheat is drilled November–December in California.
evidence.author: llm

gaps: Drainage of rice soil for a winter cereal needs a local check.

name: Alfalfa, 7–8 cuts, 4–5 year stand
tagline: What the field does today: alfalfa hay cut every 28 days from March to October.

exposed_rain_days.note: Days with heavy rain (≥ 25–50 mm) while the field is less than half covered and not flooded

why.text: This is the baseline: alfalfa planted mid-September to October, cut on a 28-day schedule after the first cut.
why.author: template

evidence.text: OpenET measured about 1,210 mm for the season; modelled crop water use is within 3%.
evidence.author: template

gaps: Number of cuts (7–8) is a typical value, not measured on this field.

name: Winter small-grain silage + silage corn
tagline: Classic dairy double crop: wheat/triticale silage off in April, corn silage by September.

exposed_rain_days.note: Days with heavy rain (≥ 25–50 mm) while the field is less than half covered and not flooded

exposure.cover_basis: modelled cover from the crop calendar

why.text: Winter small grain grows on cool-season rain, so most pumping is concentrated in the corn months of May to August.
why.author: llm

why.text: Irrigation need is about 940 mm (3.1 acre-ft/acre) against 1,320 mm for alfalfa.
why.author: llm

evidence.text: OpenET measured about 905 mm on nearby double-cropped fields; the model is within 5%.
evidence.author: llm

gaps: Silage corn and small-grain timing are typical San Joaquin Valley values, not cited.

name: Winter small-grain silage + sorghum-sudan
tagline: Same winter silage, but a summer forage that needs less water than corn.

exposed_rain_days.note: Days with heavy rain (≥ 25–50 mm) while the field is less than half covered and not flooded

exposure.cover_basis: modelled cover from the crop calendar

why.text: Sorghum-sudan gives three summer cuts with less water than corn, which matters under a pumping allocation.
why.author: llm

why.text: Irrigation need is about 720 mm (2.4 acre-ft/acre), just inside a 2.5 acre-ft/acre allocation; the high end of the range is over it.
why.author: llm

why.text: The Tulare Lake Subbasin was placed on probation on 16 April 2024, so pumping limits may tighten.
why.author: llm

evidence.text: Cover calendar 2016–2025: the field read as water for several weeks in spring 2023 when Tulare Lake re-flooded.
evidence.author: llm

evidence.text: Sorghum-sudan water savings versus corn are a widely stated extension position that still needs a UC or NRCS citation.
evidence.author: template

gaps: Sorghum-sudan water saving versus corn is not yet cited.
Number of sorghum-sudan cuts is assumed.

name: Shorter alfalfa stand + winter-cereal break
tagline: Three-year stand, then a winter cereal and a summer with no pumping before re-seeding.

exposed_rain_days.note: Days with heavy rain (≥ 25–50 mm) while the field is less than half covered and not flooded

exposure.cover_basis: modelled cover from the crop calendar

why.text: A summer with no irrigated crop is the simplest way to stay under a pumping cap in the break year.
why.author: llm

why.text: In the break year irrigation need is about 310 mm (1.0 acre-ft/acre); alfalfa is re-seeded mid-September to October.
why.author: llm

evidence.text: Alfalfa planting window of mid-September to October in the central San Joaquin Valley.
evidence.author: llm

gaps: Bare summer raises heat and dust exposure; not scored.
